newsitem.title: INDIA: India panel advises share sale in 3 state firms.
newsitem.headline: India panel advises share sale in 3 state firms.

text.p: India's Disinvestment Commission, which oversees a partial privatisation programme, on Thursday recommended sale of shares in three state-run firms in gas, food and tourism industry.

It said the government should sell 25 percent of its stake in the Gas Authority of India Ltd (GAIL), 100 percent of Modern Food Industries (India) Ltd and 74 percent or more of the India Tourism Development Corporation (ITDC).
The Commission has suggested that proceeds from the sell-off of shares in state-owned firms must be ploughed back into a separate Disinvestment Fund.

"The commission has recommended that the proceeds of disinvestment be placed separately in a Disinvestment Fund and not be fungible with other government receipts," G.V. Ramakrishna, the commission's chairman told a news conference.
The money from the Disinvestment Fund should be used to modernise loss-making state firms and extend benefits to workers in units which would be closed or restructured, he said.

India, which started partial privatisation under an economic reform programme launched in 1991, set up the commission last year to advise on a strategy for disinvestment of shares in 40 state firms. Modern Food, GAIL and ITDC are among them.
But disinvestment in the 40 firms is not expected to be taken up before two tranches of sell-offs involving other firms due in the current 1996/97 (April-March) fiscal year.
Ramakrishna submitted the first report of the commission to Industry Minister Murasoli Maran earlier on Thursday.
The commission has suggested partial sell-off of shares in GAIL should be done in both domestic and international markets depending on the market conditions.
The report recommended the government to reserve a "sizeable quantity of shares" to be offered to small investors and employees of state-run firms.
It also recommended that a high-level government panel be set-up to oversee the sell-off of shares.
Ramakrishna said the commission had also recommended more autonomy for state-owned firms in decision making, induction of professionals on their board, and forming joint ventures.
The government has set a target of raising 50 billion rupees ($1.4 billion) in 1996/97 from divestment, or the sale of partial stakes in state-run firms.
Last year, India raised 3.57 billion rupees ($99.7 million), well short of its target of 70 billion ($1.95 billion).

India has plans to sell seven percent of telecommunications firm Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL) and five percent in oil refining company Indian Oil Corp (IOC) in a first round of divestment in the current 1996/97 year.
But the government has not yet fixed a date for kicking off the first round. The government plans a second tranche but has little time because the fiscal year ends on March 31.
Ramakrishna said the commission would be making its next recommendation on more state-owned firms in March and complete its process of recommendations by October.
